title: Learning How to Remember: Memory Modality Selection for GUI Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.17928v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Recent advances in vision-language models (VLMs) have substantially improved the capabilities of GUI agents, while memory augmentation has emerged as a promising approach for reusing knowledge from past interactions. However, existing memory augmented GUI agents typically adopt a fixed representation strategy, providing retrieved experience as a static modality. It remains unclear whether a single memory modality is consistently optimal, or how modality preference changes across interaction steps. In this work, we conduct a systematic study of memory modality in VLM based GUI agents. Across GUI benchmarks, we find that the preferred memory representation is strongly step dependent. Motivated by the finding, we introduce \textbf{SwitchMem}, a routing framework that dynamically selects between textual and visual memory representations at each step. translated_title: 学习如何记忆：GUI智能体的记忆模态选择
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型的最新进展显著提升了GUI智能体的能力，而记忆增强已成为一种复用过去交互知识的有前景的方法。然而，现有的记忆增强GUI智能体通常采用固定的表示策略，将检索到的经验作为静态模态提供。目前尚不清楚单一记忆模态是否始终最优，以及模态偏好如何随交互步骤变化。在这项工作中，我们对基于视觉语言模型的GUI智能体中的记忆模态进行了系统性研究。在多个GUI基准测试中，我们发现偏好的记忆表示强烈依赖于交互步骤。受这一发现的启发，我们提出了SwitchMem，一个在每一步动态选择文本或视觉记忆表示的路由框架。在三个GUI基准测试中，SwitchMem超越了依赖单一记忆模态的记忆增强基线方法。
tldr: 本文通过系统性研究发现GUI智能体最优记忆表示随交互步骤强烈变化，并提出SwitchMem框架在每一步动态选择文本或视觉记忆模态，在三个GUI基准测试中超越了固定记忆模态的基线方法。
en_tdlr: This paper systematically reveals that the preferred memory representation for GUI agents is strongly step-dependent, and proposes SwitchMem, a routing framework that dynamically selects between textual and visual memory representations at each step, outperforming fixed-modality memory-augmented baselines across three GUI benchmarks.
